plate_findings.evidence: Article states abdominal ultrasonography confirmed hepatosplenomegaly; right panel corresponds to splenic imaging showing splenomegaly consistent with this reported finding, a classic manifestation of beta-thalassemia major.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left ultrasound panel explicitly labeled as showing hepatomegaly, which is part of the hepatosplenomegaly confirmed on abdominal ultrasonography in the beta-thalassemia major case. Hepatomegaly is a classic complication of beta-thalassemia major driven by iron overload and extramedullary hematopoiesis, but is not included in the provided findings vocabulary so is listed in proposed findings. B: Right ultrasound panel corresponding to splenic imaging demonstrating splenomegaly, which is the splenic component of the reported hepatosplenomegaly in the beta-thalassemia major case. Splenomegaly is a classic, well-documented manifestation of the disease and matches the provided findings vocabulary term beta_thalassemia_major_massive_splenomegaly.

panels.rationale: Single-panel human peripheral blood smear from a beta-thalassemia major patient, showing classic microcytic hypochromic red blood cell morphology consistent with the disease. Green arrows annotate eosinophils associated with the concurrent hypereosinophilic syndrome described in the caption and article text. No non-patient content, diagrams, or other disease imagery is present.
panels.attribution_text: Daiya et al. Concurrent Challenges in Idiopathic Hypereosinophilic Syndrome Complicating Beta-Thalassemia Major: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.56199. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: The green arrows show eosinophils observed in the peripheral smear
in_text_mentions: in level of 6.7 gm/dL, and the peripheral smear indicated microcytic hypochromic characteristics. The total leukocyte count (TLC) was approximately 117,000 cells/cumm, and the differential leukocyte count showed 60% eosinophils (with degranulation), 27% polymorphs, 3% monocytes, 10% lymphocytes, and no basophils. Platelets were adequate on the smear, and no hemoparasites were observed. The peripheral smear strongly suggested thalassemia major with significant eosinophilia (Figure 1). Sickling tests did not reveal evidence of sickle cell anemia. Laboratory investigation is mentioned in Table 1.

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of a pediatric patient with untreated beta-thalassemia major showing classical chipmunk facies (maxillary expansion, facial bone changes) and visible dental anomalies as described in the caption and in-text case description.
panels.attribution_text: Banjade and Bhandari. A Child Lost to Follow Up Carrying Beta Thalassemia Major: A Case Report.. JNMA; journal of the Nepal Medical Association 2020. doi:10.31729/jnma.5129. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Chipmunk face with dental anomaly of a child diagnosed with beta thalassemia failed to follow up.
in_text_mentions: re, with evident icterus, and yellow tinged fingernails. Decayed upper tooth, not associated with pain or swelling. Head and Neck examination showed maxillary expansion, retracted upper lip and saddle nose; all together depicting the classical “Chipmunk facies”. Also noted yellowish tinge at the junction of hard and soft palate. Intraoral examination, localized periodontitis and broken teeth in lower anterior aspect as shown (Figure 1). Her abdominal examination didn’t show and sign of enlargement of spleen. Her ophthalmologic and audiologic examination were done and were within normal limits.

plate_findings.evidence: Panel is an axial chest CT of the case; article title identifies a posterior mediastinal myelolipoma in a patient with Mediterranean anemia.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial CT of the same patient shows the captioned posterior mediastinal mass attributable to beta-thalassemia-related extramedullary hematopoietic myelolipoma. B: Axial MRI shows the posterior mediastinal paraspinal mass described in the beta-thalassemia major case. C: Coronal MRI visualizes the paraspinal/posterior mediastinal lesion in the beta-thalassemia major patient. D: H&E specimen of the lesion shows mature adipocytes and hematopoietic elements, matching the posterior mediastinal myelolipoma in the beta-thalassemia major case.
panels.attribution_text: Muriana and Negri. An unusual case of a posterior mediastinal myelolipoma in a patient with mediterranean anemia.. The Pan African medical journal 2018. doi:10.11604/pamj.2018.31.58.17041. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (A) axial chest CT-scan; (B) axial chest MRI; (C) coronal chest MRI; (D) microscopic specimen (stained with hematoxylin and eosin) of MM showing the presence of mature adipocytes (left), and hematopoietic tissue (right), consisting of erythroid and myeloid cells at different stages of differentiation. In addition, scattered megakaryocytes, rare lymphocytes and plasmacells; original magnification 40X, inset 200X

source_variant.figure_caption: (A) axial chest CT-scan; (B) axial chest MRI; (C) coronal chest MRI; (D) microscopic specimen (stained with hematoxylin and eosin) of MM showing the presence of mature adipocytes (left), and hematopoietic tissue (right), consisting of erythroid and myeloid cells at different stages of differentiation. In addition, scattered megakaryocytes, rare lymphocytes and plasmacells; original magnification 40X, inset 200X

source_variants.article_title: An unusual case of a posterior mediastinal myelolipoma in a patient with mediterranean anemia.
